title: Autotriage A/B Scheduler with Bayesian Rollback Suggester and Shadow Dry‑Run
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: reduce human triage burden for A/B experiments and speed safe rollbacks. Large experiments often produce multi-dimensional signals (latency, token-delta QA regressions, error bursts, safety flags) that are costly to aggregate manually. This PR delivers an end-to-end feature: (1) an Autotriage A/B Scheduler that places experiments into staggered cohorts with adaptive backpressure, (2) a Bayesian Rollback Suggester service that consumes telemetry and returns a rollback probability with calibrated confidence intervals, and (3) a shadow dry-run harness that mirrors production traffic for offline smoke validation before promotion.

Design summary: the scheduler extends the existing rollout controller to support an autotriage workflow: cohorts are defined as timeboxed traffic bricks (configurable per-experiment), and the scheduler monitors a signal ensemble published to the new "ab.autotriage" metrics namespace. When signals deviate beyond configured thresholds, the scheduler triggers the Rollback Suggester endpoint with the last N-window of aggregated metrics. The suggester runs a lightweight Bayesian model (beta/normal conjugates) over each metric and produces a unified rollback_score and 95% credible interval. The controller maps rollback_score + CI to action: recommend hold, reduce traffic fraction, or immediate backout.

Shadow dry-run: before any promote action, customers can opt-in to shadow dry-run which mirrors 100% of selected requests to the candidate model in a non-blocking mode. Responses are fed into the evaluator pipeline for synthetic smoke checks (response length, structured JSON conformance, hallucination heuristics, and a sampled human-like scoring function) and are included in the autotriage signals. This allows safe validation of behavioral regressions that token-based cost metrics miss.

What changed (high level): added rollout scheduler extension, new microservice (rollback_suggester), dry-run mirror adapter, console UI for "Autotriage insights", new metrics and dashboards, integration tests and canary e2e harness.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler implementation and unit tests - [x] Rollback Suggester microservice + unit tests - [x] Shadow dry-run adapter with rate controls - [x] Console panel with trend lines and suggested action - [x] End-to-end integration tests and fixture data - [x] Documentation (brief entry in rollout runbooks) - [x] Load-tested on staging with 5k rps for candidate mirroring

Testing and validation: ran full CI (lint, unit, integration), and a targeted staging run against synthetic traffic that included injected latency spikes and QA-regression payloads. The Bayesian suggester produced conservative rollback probabilities; we tuned priors to avoid noisy flips for low-volume cohorts. Synthetic human scoring was validated against 300 hand-labeled samples (AUC 0.81). Observability: added per-experiment time-series (rollback_score, rollback_ci_lower, rollback_ci_upper, signal_breakdown) and a dashboard link: https://internal.redwood.net/dashboards/autotriage/PR-598321 (dashboard requires SSO).

Risk and mitigation: the change introduces a new decision surface in the controller. To mitigate: default behavior is "recommend-only" for orgs without autopilot enabled; autopilot must be explicitly enabled per workspace. The Rollback Suggester runs with a safety cap (never auto-scale down a Dedicated pool beyond 10% without manual approval). We also added a circuit-breaker that falls back to the legacy canary behavior on downstream errors.

Release notes: Adds Autotriage A/B Scheduler, Bayesian Rollback Suggester, and Shadow Dry‑Run support for staged promotes. Autopilot mode is off by default. See rollout runbook for configuration examples.

release_notes: Adds Autotriage A/B Scheduler with a Bayesian Rollback Suggester and optional Shadow Dry‑Run mirroring. Defaults to recommend-only behavior. Autopilot must be enabled per workspace.
notes_for_ops: To enable autopilot for a workspace: set workspace.rollout.autopilot.enabled=true, configure priors at workspace.rollout.autopilot.priors. If running in Private, ensure the rollback_suggester service is deployed into the customer VPC or set the webhook to the on-prem evaluator endpoint. Monitor metrics ab.autotriage.rollback_score and ab.autotriage.signal_breakdown for early indicators.
backout_plan: If a regression is detected in production: (1) run the autotriage dashboard -> select experiment -> press 'Backout' to immediate reduce to 0% (console triggers rollout controller), (2) run snapshot replay from the rollback journal, (3) open a hotfix PR against main for candidate fixes. Autopilot mode will not auto-backout without explicit enablement.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: the bailouts default to recommend-only and the suggester uses conservative priors to avoid flip-flopping on low-traffic cohorts. The instrumentation added here will also help build future auto-heal policies.
